editorial:
Imagine you are living in the mid 90s, surrounded by CDs and music magazines, and your heart just got crushed. That is exactly where you meet Ben, a guy whose world falls apart after a bad breakup. He works for a big music magazine, and since he is feeling low, he decides to stop chasing love and start focusing on himself. The vibe is very lighthearted and nostalgic, capturing that specific era of music culture. You will find yourself rooting for Ben as he tries to figure out how to be happy on his own while dealing with the chaos of his job and his emotions.

What really makes this work is the funny chemistry between the characters and the breezy pace that keeps you interested. It is not a heavy drama, but it feels real because everyone has been through a breakup. The only downside is that it follows some old-school rom-com tropes, but that is part of the charm. If you want something feel-good, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for those who love movie memorabilia.
endingExplained: After spending the movie trying to stay single and independent, Ben eventually realizes that being alone isn't actually what he wants. He discovers that his growth as a person allows him to find a healthier kind of love. In the final scenes, he stops running from his feelings and reunites with the love of his life. The story wraps up with a sweet, happy ending where he balances his passion for music with a stable relationship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 90s nostalgia and cute romantic comedies.
